    Middle East — Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Iraq, Iran; with secondary impact on global energy markets and US political landscape

Temporal focus:

    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — escalation risks, Hormuz/Bab el-Mandeb control, US midterm political pressure, Iran-Gulf talks in Oman
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — potential Iranian strategic control of both Arabian Peninsula chokepoints, structural oil supply disruption

Synopsis:
    Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline (4–5 mbd, ~4–5% of global supply) after a drone strike traced to Iranian-backed Iraqi militias, while Houthi rebels — with direct Iranian Revolutionary Guard guidance — seized Perim Island at the Bab el-Mandeb strait. Combined with ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruptions from the US-Iran war, both key energy chokepoints flanking the Arabian Peninsula are now threatened. Oil prices have crossed $100/bbl. Saudi crude output is at 30-year lows. MBS called Trump twice requesting military intervention; Washington declined direct action, offering intelligence support only. Iran is conditioning diplomacy on full acceptance of its terms. The dual chokepoint threat represents a potential Iranian strategic masterstroke that could reshape global energy flows and amplify pressure on the Trump administration ahead of November congressional elections.
